title: Falcon Systems Launches Falcon 5000 Series for Quantum Secure Networks
html:
Insider Brief

  • Falcon Systems has launched the Falcon 5000 Series, a new generation of its MDI-QKD portfolio designed to support scalable Quantum Secure Networks across critical infrastructure.
  • The series combines QKD nodes, connectivity hubs and optical switches with features including dual-homing, inter-hub connectivity, tamper detection and redundant power and cooling systems.
  • Forschungszentrum Jülich will be the launch customer, using the system to investigate the integration of quantum key distribution into power system communication networks.

PRESS RELEASE — Falcon Systems, the Netherlands-based leader building the infrastructure for Quantum Secure Networks (QSN), announces the launch of the Falcon® 5000 Series, the next generation of its proven Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD) portfolio. The new Series combines secure-by-design technology, scalable network connectivity and industry-grade hardware that enable resilient Quantum Secure Networks across critical digital infrastructure.

As Europe prepares for the long-term security implications of quantum computing, governments, telecommunications operators and critical infrastructure providers face a growing need to protect sensitive communications across increasingly interconnected networks. Quantum Secure Networks (QSN) provide an important layer of long-term cryptographic security, complementing existing encryption infrastructure and post-quantum cryptography (PQC).

Addressing this need, the Falcon 5000 Series builds on the field-proven Falcon 4000 Series and deployments across Europe, introducing enhanced physical security, operational reliability and scalable network connectivity. Forschungszentrum Jülich, one of Europe’s leading interdisciplinary research centers, will be the launch customer for the Falcon 5000 Series, marking another milestone in Falcon Systems’ expanding pan-European quantum network footprint.

“Europe has an opportunity to lead in the next generation of secure digital infrastructure, but technological leadership must translate into solutions that can be deployed and scaled. Our Falcon 5000 Series marks another step in strengthening Europe’s technological sovereignty and accelerating the wider commercial adoption of Quantum Secure Networks,” said Dr. Ingrid Romijn, CEO and Co-Founder of Falcon Systems.

Quantum security built for network scale

Falcon Systems’ MDI-QKD technology eliminates detector-side-channel vulnerabilities from the QKD security model, delivering an inherent security advantage over conventional QKD architectures. The Falcon 5000 Series retains this proven security foundation while introducing enhanced physical protection, including integrated tamper detection and security monitoring to meet the requirements of sensitive and mission-critical infrastructure.

Unlike conventional point-to-point QKD architectures, Falcon Systems’ network-first architecture connects an expanding number of QKD Nodes through one or more shared Connectivity Hubs. This reduces dedicated pairwise fiber requirements and network complexity, enabling more cost-effective expansion across distributed sites.

Designed for long-term network operations, the Falcon 5000 Series introduces redundant, hot-swappable power and cooling systems, enhanced serviceability, integrated tamper detection and hardware-based protection of sensitive key material. These improvements strengthen operational reliability, maintainability and physical security of the MDI-QKD devices.

“The future of quantum secure communications is not about connecting individual locations, but building networks that can scale, adapt and remain resilient as they grow. With new features like dual-homing and inter-hub connectivity, the Falcon 5000 Series extends our network-first architecture towards interconnected Quantum Secure Networks (QSN) designed to meet the demands of critical digital infrastructure,” said Remon Berrevoets, CTIO of Falcon Systems.

Scalable and resilient network infrastructure

The Series comprises three core hardware components, the Falcon Connectivity Hub (CH5000), Falcon QKD Node (QN5000) and Falcon Quantum Optical Switch (QOS5000). Together, they provide the MDI-QKD infrastructure for secure key generation, shared quantum network connectivity and flexible optical routing.

The Falcon® 5000 Series

Engineered for integration with existing telecom and data center environments, the Falcon 5000 Series enables network operators and infrastructure providers to expand quantum secure connectivity services, including Quantum Secure Networks as a Service (QSN-as-a-Service), across metropolitan, national and cross-border infrastructure.

“The Falcon 5000 Series represents an important addition to our quantum communication research infrastructure, enabling us to investigate the integration of quantum key distribution into power system communication networks. Its scalable architecture provides a valuable platform for evaluating secure and resilient communications in critical energy infrastructure,” said Dr. Daniele Carta, Head of Control Solutions Department at Forschungszentrum Jülich.

The collaboration marks a significant milestone in the commercial introduction of Falcon Systems’ next-generation MDI-QKD infrastructure, further extending its pan-European network footprint through a leading center for quantum research and advanced computing.

An integrated technology portfolio for Quantum Secure Networks

Complementing the Falcon 5000 Series, the Falcon Key Manager provides secure cryptographic key lifecycle management and key delivery, while the Falcon Domain Controller enables centralised quantum network management and orchestration.

Together, the Falcon 5000 Series, Falcon Key Manager and Falcon Domain Controller provide the integrated technologies required to deploy, manage and scale Quantum Secure Networks (QSN). Standards-based interoperability, including ETSI GS QKD 004, 014, 020 and SKIP, enables integration with existing telecom, encryption and third-party key management infrastructure.

European technology for sovereign digital infrastructure

Designed, developed and manufactured in Europe, the Falcon 5000 Series reinforces Falcon Systems’ commitment to European technological sovereignty and trusted communication infrastructure.

“Our collaboration with Falcon Systems reflects a shared commitment to strengthening the security of critical energy infrastructure through scalable and interoperable European quantum communication technologies. The Falcon 5000 Series brings together proven MDI-QKD technology and industry-grade capabilities, making it a valuable addition to our research infrastructure for secure power system monitoring and control,” said Dr. Daniele Carta, Head of Control Solutions Department at Forschungszentrum Jülich.

For European government, defence and critical infrastructure organisations, access to trusted, European-developed quantum security technology is important for long-term digital resilience and strategic autonomy. The Falcon 5000 Series supports these priorities with sovereign, interoperable infrastructure designed for national and cross-border Quantum Communication Infrastructure (QCI) programmes.

Building the foundation for future quantum connectivity

The underlying Connectivity Hub offers potential applications beyond Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), including future connectivity between quantum processors, computers, sensors and emerging quantum devices.

“The future of quantum technology will depend not only on the capabilities of individual devices, but on how we connect them. The network infrastructure we are developing today lays the foundation for the next generation of interconnected quantum systems,” said Dr. Joshua Slater, CTO of Falcon Systems.

The Falcon 5000 Series reinforces Falcon Systems’ commitment to operational Quantum Secure Networks (QSN) today and its longer-term vision for interconnected quantum infrastructure.
